title: Amendment 8: Election and Removal of County Sheriffs

context.text: Placed on the ballot by the General Assembly as CCS HCS SS SJR 87, sponsored by Sen. Jill Carter (R-Granby). Senate 24-7 (March 25, 2026); the House amended it (100-47, May 11, per the House Journal); the final conference committee substitute passed the House 95-46 and the Senate 24-9 on May 15, 2026. St. Louis City, St. Louis County and St. Charles County are excluded from the amendment's election requirement.

question.text: Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to support law enforcement by preserving the right of citizens to elect a county sheriff, prohibiting the removal of a county sheriff except by a writ of quo warranto, and recognizing the office of sheriff as part of the administration of justice? State and local governmental entities estimate no costs or savings.

summary.text: Per the Secretary of State's Fair Ballot Language, a yes vote requires counties to elect a sheriff every four years (currently required by statute), places in the Constitution provisions on sheriffs’ duties that are currently in statute, and provides that an elected sheriff may be removed only through a writ of quo warranto initiated by the Attorney General. St. Louis Public Radio notes most sheriffs, including in St. Louis, are already elected, so the amendment would write that process into the Constitution. State and local governmental entities estimate no costs or savings.

measure.yesMeans: “A ‘yes’ vote will amend the Missouri Constitution to require counties to: elect a sheriff every four years, which is currently required by statute; place in the Constitution provisions regarding sheriffs’ duties that are currently provided by statute; and provide that an elected sheriff may be removed from office only through a writ of quo warranto initiated by the Attorney General.” (Secretary of State, Fair Ballot Language)
measure.noMeans: “A ‘no’ vote will not amend the Missouri Constitution. Current Missouri statutes providing for the election of county sheriffs to four-year terms and governing their duties and removal will remain in effect unless changed by law.” (Secretary of State, Fair Ballot Language)

argumentsFor.text: Sen. Jill Carter (R-Granby), the sponsor: “At its core, this bill is about one simple but powerful idea: accountability to the people. Sheriffs in Missouri should be chosen by and held accountable to the voters of their county — not appointed, insulated or controlled by political bodies.”
Sen. Jill Carter (R-Granby), the sponsor: "We're not giving them any more power, any more authority than they currently statutorily have."

argumentsAgainst.text: Vicky Wors, Democratic candidate for Missouri Senate District 26, on her campaign site: “The most consequential part of Amendment 8 concerns how a sheriff could be removed from office. Under current Missouri law, county prosecutors have authority to pursue the removal of certain local officials for willful or fraudulent misconduct, corruption, or neglect of duty. Amendment 8 would take that authority away from local prosecutors and require any effort to remove a sheriff to begin through a court proceeding initiated exclusively by the Missouri attorney general.”

Boone County Sheriff Dwayne Carey: "I think a sheriff can be removed at a local level." He said a county judge, elected by the same constituents as the sheriff, should have the authority to remove a sheriff who acts illegally or unethically.

currentLaw.text: The office of sheriff is outlined in state law rather than the Constitution; state statute requires counties to elect a sheriff to a four-year term and governs the sheriff's duties and removal, and those statutes stay in effect on a "no" vote (Fair Ballot Language). Under current law, a county prosecutor or the attorney general can initiate a quo warranto action seeking a sheriff's removal; Amendment 8 would reserve that authority to the attorney general. The amendment would not apply to St. Louis City, St. Louis County or St. Charles County.

fiscalImpact.text: Official ballot statement: State and local governmental entities estimate no costs or savings. The Fair Ballot Language adds that, if passed, the measure will not increase or decrease taxes.

supporters.text: State Sen. Jill Carter (R-Granby), sponsor of the joint resolution.
State Rep. Bennie Cook (R-Houston), who handled the resolution in the House.
Osage County Sheriff Michael Bonham, who said Missouri should enshrine the sheriff's authority as more than 30 states do.

opponents.text: Missouri Democratic Party, which urged a "no" vote.
Vicky Wors, Democratic candidate for Missouri Senate District 26.
State Rep. Bryant Wolfin (R-Ste. Genevieve), who voted against the resolution in the House, saying it did not go far enough to empower "constitutional sheriffs."

researchNotes: Official ballot title, fiscal statement and Fair Ballot Language are quoted verbatim (machine-checked) from the Missouri Secretary of State's certified-measure page. Missouri publishes no state voter pamphlet with pro/con arguments, so arguments are from campaign materials and news reports. No registered campaign for or against Amendment 8 was found; the opposing argument is from a legislative candidate's own site. Ballotpedia lists State Rep. Will Jobe (D) as an opponent but no statement from him was fetched. The 100-47 House vote on May 11 and the 95-46 final House vote are from the House Journals (Ballotpedia lists 85-56 for May 11, which does not match the Journal); the Senate 24-7 (March 25) is from Ballotpedia and the final Senate 24-9 from St. Louis Public Radio. No campaignFinance field: ABC17 reported on Oct. 15, 2026 that no political action committees had formed for or against Amendment 8.
